violations.title: Receiving Temperature, Eggs
violations.observation: Raw shelled eggs are received at inadequate temperatures. Observed Raw shell eggs at room temperature 73F
violations.corrective_action: Raw eggs shall be received in refrigerated equipment that maintains an ambient air temperature of 45F or less. CFM relocated Raw shell eggs to walk in refrigerator

violations.title: Receiving Temperature, Refrigerated Foods
violations.observation: The following refrigerated food item(s) is received at inadequate temperatures: Observed raw chicken at 48F
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated time/temperature control for safety food shall be at a temperature of 41F or below when received.CFM relocated chicken to the freezer

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: Observed cooked lamb and cooked chicken in unit # 2 and red sauce, cooked lamb and cooked chicken in unit # in unit # 1 and cooked lamb in unit # 3 with no preparation or expiration date.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CFM date marked all foos items with the preparation date.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: Observed utensil store in metal container in standing water at 73F
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. CFM washed, rinsed and sanitized utensil and stored them in 140F water

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Observed heavy cream ( top) in unit # 3 at 46F, Heavy cream at seasoning rack at 68F
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CFM discarded heavy creams

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked:Observed cooked chicken, cooked beef, roasted eggplant, cooked okra in unit # 1 with no date labels
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. CFM labeled all TCS foods with the preparation date.
